[NCBK.1.1] Every callback an integrator registers on an engine (the stream,
metric, log and call callbacks, and the two cache callbacks) has the **same
three-argument shape and returns `ds_result_t`**. Only the payload type varies
between areas: the engine handle comes first, a `const` pointer to what
happened second, and the integrator's own context pointer third. The cache set
callback's payload is the write ([NSTG.2.3]).

That uniformity is what the rest of this section rests on. The argument roles
([NCBK.1.2]-[NCBK.1.4]), the meaning of a non-OK return ([NCBK.1.5]), the
lifetime of pointers reachable from the payload ([NCBK.1.6]), the thread the
call arrives on ([NCBK.1.7]), and how registration and replacement behave
([NCBK.1.9]) are stated **once, here**, and hold for every registered callback.
An integrator who has learned one signature has learned all of them.

A visitor that an enumerating read takes as an argument, and calls before it
returns, is not a registered callback, and has the shape its call declares:
the Rete visitors return nothing ([IARC.1.12]). The re-entry rule binds inside
a visitor as inside a callback ([RARC.13.17]).

The concrete type for each area is named in that area's own clause, and every one is declared in `runtime/include/libds.h`.
